final_observable_contract: For a recognized literal execution candidate on the local terminal backend, with security.malware.enabled and execution_gate enabled and no explicit allowlist registration, an authoritative malicious finding plus another engine error must not authorize terminal execution. This is a downstream preservation contract, not a completed U1 commit mapping.
downstream_owner: SecurityService decision and terminal execution gate
windows_constraints: No live malware download or Defender disablement
Synthetic findings and a mocked terminal executor are not native scanner or OS containment proof
The terminal gate scans recognized literal references with known suffixes; indirect execution forms and candidates outside this parser are not covered by this claim
The terminal caller invokes this gate only for the local backend, and both malware and execution_gate settings must be enabled
Explicit hash or path allowlisting can permit execution despite an engine error; a path registration may also apply after file content changes
rationale: D0 checks scanner errors before the malicious score, producing SCAN_ERROR, and its gate blocks only MALICIOUS. The local feature separates file verdict, engine health and execution decision, then blocks BLOCK and REVIEW. Reimplementing this already present fix would risk regression.
public_compatibility_delta: When the local terminal security gate is enabled, D0 could allow a recognized malicious candidate when another engine failed. The local feature blocks that candidate without an explicit allowlist registration, while retaining the allowlist route and a clean-authoritative success case.
